entities.name: PMID:27489225
observations: Mouse disc explants and human disc cells showed autonomous PER2 rhythms; amplitude declined with age. IL-1β abolished rhythms, while TNF-α did not under tested conditions. Disc-specific Bmal1 deletion caused age-related degeneration.

entities.name: PMID:37495193
observations: Col2a1-Bmal1 knockout in mice disrupted circadian transcripts and was associated with age-related annulus fibrosus matrix and cell-fate changes.

entities.name: PMID:34934193
observations: Degenerated human and rat nucleus pulposus showed reduced BMAL1/CLOCK; mechanical loading disrupted clock rhythms and matrix genes, and BMAL1 overexpression partly rescued matrix-gene effects.

entities.name: PMID:35922862
observations: IL-1β-associated clock dampening and Bmal1 knockdown were linked to NP-cell inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and degeneration; NRF2 activation attenuated effects.

entities.name: Intrinsic IVD clock
observations: PER2 reporter rhythms persisted in mouse disc explants for over five days (period 23.93±0.10 h), occurred in annulus fibrosus and nucleus pulposus, and were also observed in human disc cells.

entities.name: Age cytokine sensitivity
observations: Disc circadian amplitude dampened with mouse aging; IL-1β abolished rhythms while TNF-α did not under the tested conditions.

entities.name: Clock-linked degeneration
observations: Disc-specific Bmal1 deletion caused age-related degeneration in mice; degenerated tissue showed dampened clock markers, and mechanical stress or IL-1β-linked clock disruption impaired matrix/inflammatory homeostasis.
